title: Kubernetes & Containers
summary: The vocabulary of running production workloads on Kubernetes — containers, pods, deployments, services, storage, security, GitOps, the ecosystem (service meshes, observability), and the frontier (WASM, eBPF, serverless K8s).

volatileChapters.reason: Service mesh landscape (Istio Ambient, Cilium service mesh) churns quarterly; observability stack (Prometheus ecosystem, OTel) evolves rapidly; autoscaler choices (KEDA, Karpenter) gain features per quarter.
WASM workloads, eBPF dataplanes, and AI-augmented scheduling are the fastest-moving frontier in K8s. Native sidecar status and DRA evolve per K8s release.

chapters.title: From Containers to Orchestration
chapters.summary: Container primitives (Linux namespaces, cgroups, OCI), why orchestrators exist, and the Kubernetes architecture — control plane (API server, scheduler, controller manager, etcd) and data plane (kubelet, runtime, kube-proxy).

chapters.title: Pods, Deployments, ReplicaSets
chapters.summary: The atomic unit (pod) through the higher-level abstractions — pod lifecycle, init/sidecar/ephemeral containers, ReplicaSets, Deployments, rolling updates, rollouts, and graceful shutdown.

chapters.title: Services and Networking
chapters.summary: How pods talk to each other and the outside world — Service types (ClusterIP/NodePort/LoadBalancer/Headless), kube-proxy, CNI plugins, CoreDNS, Ingress controllers, NetworkPolicy, and Gateway API.

chapters.title: Storage and StatefulSets
chapters.summary: Persistent storage for K8s — PersistentVolumes, PVCs, StorageClasses, the CSI driver model, dynamic provisioning, and StatefulSets for clustered databases and other workloads needing stable identity.

chapters.title: ConfigMaps, Secrets, and the 12-Factor App
chapters.summary: Configuration and secrets management — ConfigMaps and Secrets, mounting strategies, immutable variants, External Secrets Operator, Sealed Secrets, SOPS, and KMS-backed encryption at rest.

chapters.title: Scheduling and Resource Management
chapters.summary: How the scheduler places pods — requests vs limits, QoS classes, node selectors, affinity/anti-affinity, taints/tolerations, topology spread, resource quotas, LimitRange, and the VPA/HPA distinction.

chapters.title: Health, Readiness, and Probes
chapters.summary: Keeping workloads healthy — liveness/readiness/startup probes (HTTP, TCP, exec, gRPC), Pod Disruption Budgets, preStop hooks, terminationGracePeriodSeconds, and the mechanics of graceful shutdown.

chapters.title: Workload Patterns
chapters.summary: The canonical patterns — sidecar, ambassador, adapter, init containers, Jobs, CronJobs, DaemonSets, leader election, work queue, static pods, priority/preemption, and native sidecars (1.29+).

chapters.title: Operators and Custom Resources
chapters.summary: Extending Kubernetes — CRDs and Custom Resources, the controller pattern, the reconciliation loop, Operator SDK / Kubebuilder, finalizers, owner references, admission webhooks, and operator capability levels.

chapters.title: Security and RBAC
chapters.summary: Securing the cluster — ServiceAccounts, RBAC, Pod Security Standards, SecurityContext, admission controllers, OPA Gatekeeper, Kyverno, image signing with Sigstore, NetworkPolicy for security, and secrets encryption.

chapters.title: Multi-Cluster and GitOps
chapters.summary: Beyond a single cluster — multi-cluster service discovery, GitOps with ArgoCD and Flux, Helm and Kustomize, App-of-Apps pattern, drift detection, and environment promotion via Git PRs.

chapters.title: The Ecosystem
chapters.summary: The cloud-native landscape around K8s — service meshes (Istio, Linkerd, Cilium, Ambient mesh), observability (Prometheus, OpenTelemetry, Grafana, Loki), autoscaling (KEDA, Karpenter), runtime security (Falco), and cert-manager.

chapters.title: Kubernetes in 2026+
chapters.summary: The frontier — WASM workloads (SpinKube, Krustlet), eBPF dataplanes, AI-augmented scheduling, serverless K8s (vCluster, Knative), confidential containers, Dynamic Resource Allocation (DRA), and multi-tenancy patterns.
